purpose_clarity.justification: States the specific verb and resource (create, change, delete tags) and routes reads elsewhere. It clearly distinguishes itself from list_entities and the other manage_ tools.

usage_guidelines.justification: Names the explicit alternative for reads (list_entities with type tag) and notes that other fields are refused. Each action lists its required inputs and refusals.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Goes well beyond the annotations: create on an existing name (even a deleted one) updates it and returns the id, delete is a soft-delete that disappears from listings, and unknown ids are refused. It also states Writes up front.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 80%, so the schema already documents the fields. The description adds only the no-leading-hash rule for tag and the at-least-one-field rule for update, which is modest additional value.

conciseness_structure.justification: Front-loads purpose and action routing, then compacts each action into a short clause. Dense but every clause carries a rule, so little is wasted.

contextual_completeness.justification: Even without an output schema it documents the return shape for each action and the refusal cases. An agent has enough to call it correctly.

summary: A strong, dense definition that routes reads to a sibling, spells out per-action requirements and failures, and documents return shapes. Minor gap: parameter semantics mostly rest on the schema.

purpose_clarity.justification: Clearly states it creates, upserts, changes or deletes budget rules and that one action is picked. It is distinct from list_entities and manage_schedules.

usage_guidelines.justification: Names the read alternative (list_entities type rule) and explicitly redirects deleting a schedule-owned rule to manage_schedules delete. It also gives the per-action field requirements.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Discloses a lot beyond annotations: the field-by-op compatibility matrix, id existence validation before any write, create_batch non-atomicity with per-item failures and a retry caution, upsert matching semantics, and that delete cannot be undone.

parameter_semantics.justification: Coverage is 86%, but the description supplies substantial semantic detail the terse schema lacks: which ops apply to which fields, the default conditions_op, camelCase batch keys, and unsent-field behavior on update.

conciseness_structure.justification: It is one very long run-on block; the content is largely necessary but hard to scan. Breaking the op matrix and batch caveats into structure would help.

contextual_completeness.justification: Documents return shapes for all five actions and the important failure and retry behaviors. That is enough for correct invocation of a complex tool.

summary: Very thorough and genuinely informative, especially on condition ops and batch non-atomicity. The main weakness is presentation: a dense single paragraph that is difficult to parse.

purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb and resource with scope noted (one-off or recurring schedules) and a single action selector. Clearly separate from list_entities and manage_rules.

usage_guidelines.justification: Points reads to list_entities type schedule and previews to the same with schedule_id. It also states per-action requirements and which fields cannot be set.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Adds real context beyond annotations: delete also removes the driving rule but leaves created transactions, a new date replaces the stored recurrence, completed and next_date cannot be set, and amount_op isbetween requires an object amount.

parameter_semantics.justification: Coverage is 90%, but the description adds useful semantics: integer cents with negative outflows, the amount_op constraints, and the recurrence object shape. It goes beyond the schema on interaction rules.

conciseness_structure.justification: Front-loads purpose, then compactly handles create, update and delete. It is long but reasonably ordered and most sentences carry rules.

contextual_completeness.justification: Return shapes for each action and the destructive consequences of delete are documented. Sufficient for a 10-parameter tool with no output schema.

summary: Well-scoped and behaviorally explicit, particularly around delete side effects and recurrence updates. Parameter and conciseness are strong though not flawless.

purpose_clarity.justification: Names the resource and enumerates the specific mutations (amounts, carryover, hold, transfers, note) under one action selector. It is clearly distinct from the read tool list_budget_months and manage_budget_files.

usage_guidelines.justification: Explicitly routes reads to list_budget_months and points switching, import and export to manage_budget_files and category notes to manage_categories. It also states per-action requirements.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Excellent disclosure beyond annotations: hold may hold less than requested and ADDS to the buffer, set_amount_batch is non-atomic with partial application, transfer can leave the source lowered if the second write fails, and reset_hold is safe to repeat.

parameter_semantics.justification: Coverage is 89%, but the description adds meaningful constraints: cents are integers, hold and transfer amounts must be greater than 0, from and to categories must differ, and batch item shape. Substantially more than the schema alone.

conciseness_structure.justification: A single very long paragraph covering seven actions; the density and run-on structure hurt scanability even though most content is warranted.

contextual_completeness.justification: Documents return shapes for every action, including partial results and failure envelopes, plus retry guidance. Complete despite the absent output schema.

summary: Behaviorally rich and complete, with strong warnings about non-atomic operations and clamping. Its main flaw is the dense single-block presentation.

purpose_clarity.justification: States the three specific operations (switch active budget, import a file, export active budget) with an action selector. It is clearly separate from budget-file listing and month management.

usage_guidelines.justification: Routes listing to list_entities type budget_file and month edits to manage_budget_months. It also gives per-action input rules and explicitly says to confirm before importing over real data.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Discloses critical behavior beyond annotations: switch is session-only yet remembered as a preference, import may REPLACE a budget copy and loads a budget outside the configured list, and export overwrites a same-named file without returning contents.

parameter_semantics.justification: Coverage is 83%, but the description clarifies exactly one of path or base64, filename restrictions and append behavior, and the default import type. Useful additions over the schema.

conciseness_structure.justification: Front-loaded purpose followed by structured per-action detail and return shapes. Long but mostly earns its length, with warnings placed where they matter.

contextual_completeness.justification: Return shapes for switch, import and export are documented, along with failure and permission cases. Sufficient for a destructive multi-mode tool with no output schema.

summary: A high-quality definition that surfaces the destructive and non-obvious consequences of import and export. Concision is good given the complexity, though still long.
